From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morales <alex@kilnanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC traffic stress window — need to shift kickoff by one day

Alex —

Quick note ahead of the POC kickoff: we had the working session penciled for Tue 14th (1:00–4:00pm PT) to cover prompt review, routing rules, and a light load dry-run. Two things I want to confirm before sending a calendar invite:

- Can you confirm the throughput target you care most about for the stress window (RPS, sustained tokens/sec, or concurrent sessions)? We saw a range during discovery notes (100–500 concurrent), want the authoritative number.
- Do you want the team to run a short latency SLO sweep (p95/p99) during the window, or focus purely on throughput?

We can shift the kickoff by a day if that helps your calendar — Marissa and I are flexible Wed 15th the same time. If Wed works, we’ll attach the runbook and a short agenda (30m: prompts/requirements, 120m: routed load tests, 30m: next steps).

Attaching a draft agenda and the load harness config we plan to use. Let me know which day/time you prefer and the primary throughput target so we can size the instances.

Thanks,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Rishi —

Thanks for the note. Wed 15th the same time (1:00–4:00pm PT) actually works better for our engineering leads — can we move it a day? I pulled together the baseline throughput numbers:

- Primary target: 300 concurrent sessions (burst to 500 for short spikes)
- Preferred metrics: p95 latency under 350ms, p99 under 800ms for the main route
- Test harness: we can run two scenarios (prompt-heavy and routing-heavy), both will be in the spreadsheet I attached below.

Procurement is looping in to confirm the intake steps for access and any network peering we need; they asked for a 48-hour heads-up on IP whitelisting.

One ask: if you have a recent run showing typical token-cost at those loads, could you include that in the kickoff materials?

Appreciate the flexibility — Alex

--
Alex Morales
Head of Integrations, Kiln Analytics
alex@kilnanalytics.com
[Attachment: throughput-targets-kiln.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]

Alex — great, Wed 7/15 works for our engineering squad. Updated plan and a few operational notes below.

Agenda (final):
- 01:00–01:30 PM PT — Intro & prompt routing review (include sample prompt sets)
- 01:30–03:30 PM PT — Load scenarios: routing-heavy then prompt-heavy (we'll run two 30m sustained intervals and 10m spike tests)
- 03:30–04:00 PM PT — Results, tuning actions, next steps

Operational checklist (please review):
- IP whitelist: send the list of egress IPs you need whitelisted; procurement mentioned 48-hour window
- Access: we will provision a short-lived token and a dedicated model variant for the session
- Cost estimate: attached a quick token-cost ballpark for the two scenarios (see redwood-load-harness notes)

Attachments: runbook link and harness config attached. If you want us to run an initial 15m smoke test before the session starts (12:40–12:55 PT) we can do that — good to catch network issues early.

I’m attaching the runbook folder (Drive link) and the harness YAML to this thread. I’ll send the calendar invite in the next message.

Thanks — Marissa
